descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the OpenShift Router. When a Route has `insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy` set to Allow, the HTTP frontend does not remove `X-SSL-Client-*` headers from incoming requests. This allows an unauthenticated attacker to send plain HTTP requests with crafted `X-SSL-Client-*` headers. As a result, backends relying on these headers for mutual TLS (Transport Layer Security) authentication can be bypassed, enabling the attacker to impersonate client certificate identities.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en el OpenShift Router. Cuando una Ruta tiene 'insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy' configurado en Allow, el frontend HTTP no elimina los encabezados 'X-SSL-Client-*' de las solicitudes entrantes. Esto permite a un atacante no autenticado enviar solicitudes HTTP en texto plano con encabezados 'X-SSL-Client-*' manipulados. Como resultado, los backends que dependen de estos encabezados para la autenticación mutua TLS (Transport Layer Security) pueden ser eludidos, permitiendo al atacante suplantar identidades de certificados de cliente.

A flaw was found in OpenShift Container Platform. Completed pods with restartPolicy: Never do not count toward ResourceQuota pod limits, and Kubernetes events are not quota-scoped. A non-privileged user who can create pods in a namespace can exploit this to generate a large volume of events that accumulate in etcd, causing API server performance degradation across the cluster.

Se encontró una falla en OpenShift Container Platform. Los pods completados con restartPolicy: Never no cuentan para los límites de pods de ResourceQuota, y los eventos de Kubernetes no están sujetos a cuota. Un usuario no privilegiado que puede crear pods en un namespace puede explotar esto para generar un gran volumen de eventos que se acumulan en etcd, causando degradación del rendimiento del servidor API en todo el clúster.
Overly permissive configuration settings on cloud storage containers expose active telemetry information publicly to the internet.
Configuraciones excesivamente permisivas en contenedores de almacenamiento en la nube exponen información de telemetría activa públicamente a internet.
The debugging routine SCREEN_CLICK(5053) enables a connection to skip the standard device login prompt entirely and directly enter an interactive shell interface.

La rutina de depuración SCREEN_CLICK(5053) permite que una conexión omita completamente la solicitud de inicio de sesión estándar del dispositivo y entre directamente en una interfaz de shell interactiva.
Internal multimedia session archives are accessible without authentication, exacerbated by loose Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) rules that allow cross-site theft.
Los archivos internos de sesiones multimedia son accesibles sin autenticación, exacerbado por reglas laxas de Intercambio de Recursos de Origen Cruzado (CORS) que permiten el robo entre sitios.
Crucial management API endpoints for cellular eSIM allocation do not validate caller authorization, allowing remote profiles to be rewritten or deleted.
Puntos finales cruciales de la API de gestión para la asignación de eSIM celulares no validan la autorización del llamador, permitiendo que los perfiles remotos sean reescritos o eliminados.
Leftover debug modules contain fixed credentials for internal AWS Cognito test sandboxes, risking asset exploitation.
Módulos de depuración remanentes contienen credenciales fijas para sandboxes de prueba internos de AWS Cognito, arriesgando la explotación de activos.
System log files output unencrypted SMTP server authentication passwords alongside sensitive employee corporate identification data.
Los archivos de registro del sistema muestran contraseñas de autenticación del servidor SMTP sin cifrar junto con datos sensibles de identificación corporativa de empleados.
Incoming VPN network profile settings fail to process special characters safely, enabling command injection via malicious config files.
Los ajustes de perfiles de red VPN entrantes no logran procesar caracteres especiales de forma segura, permitiendo la inyección de comandos a través de archivos de configuración maliciosos.
The system Binder boundary accepts unverified pass-through AT commands, giving local applications the power to read baseband files or disable cellular connectivity.
El límite Binder del sistema acepta comandos AT de paso sin verificar, dando a las aplicaciones locales el poder de leer archivos de banda base o deshabilitar la conectividad celular.
High-risk TrustAllCerts routines disable standard TLS certificate validation. Combined with hard-coded DES symmetric encryption keys, a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) actor could decrypt network traffic.

Las rutinas TrustAllCerts de alto riesgo deshabilitan la validación estándar de certificados TLS. Combinado con claves de cifrado simétrico DES codificadas de forma rígida, un actor man-in-the-middle (MitM) podría descifrar el tráfico de red.
Broadcast events allow malicious software to rewrite the device's default Mobile Device Management (MDM) endpoint address, shifting administrative ownership to an external attacker.

Los eventos de difusión permiten que software malicioso reescriba la dirección de punto final predeterminada de Gestión de Dispositivos Móviles (MDM) del dispositivo, transfiriendo la propiedad administrativa a un atacante externo.
The device encrypts data using AES-CBC with static zero-filled Initialization Vectors (IVs), making it susceptible to replay attacks and known-plaintext decryption.
El dispositivo cifra datos usando AES-CBC con Vectores de Inicialización (IVs) estáticos rellenados con ceros, haciéndolo susceptible a ataques de repetición y descifrado de texto plano conocido.
Leftover engineering diagnostics and factory-level diagnostic software remain exposed on retail builds, giving malicious apps write privileges to internal NVRAM registers.

Diagnósticos de ingeniería residuales y software de diagnóstico a nivel de fábrica permanecen expuestos en versiones comerciales, otorgando a las aplicaciones maliciosas privilegios de escritura en registros internos de NVRAM.
Weak validation logic within device dissociation API routines allows a remote entity to forcefully unbind unrelated user endpoints, causing severe denial of service.

Lógica de validación débil dentro de las rutinas de la API de disociación de dispositivos permite a una entidad remota desvincular forzosamente puntos finales de usuario no relacionados, causando una denegación de servicio grave.
The account validation endpoint /v1/User/validate returns comprehensive user profile data sheets, which can be crawled by iterating predictable identification strings.
El endpoint de validación de cuentas /v1/User/validate devuelve hojas de datos de perfil de usuario completas, que pueden ser rastreadas iterando cadenas de identificación predecibles.
The /v1/Plan service relies entirely on a shared global API token for full administrative management, allowing arbitrary creation of zero-cost network access plans.
El servicio /v1/Plan se basa completamente en un token API global compartido para la gestión administrativa completa, permitiendo la creación arbitraria de planes de acceso a la red de costo cero.
The web administration panel binds broadly to the public IPv6 address space on port [::]:8080 without default firewall limits, making internal API endpoints reachable over the WAN.

El panel de administración web se enlaza ampliamente con el espacio de direcciones IPv6 público en el puerto [::]:8080 sin límites predeterminados del cortafuegos, haciendo que los puntos finales de la API internos sean accesibles a través de la WAN.
The registration path /v1/account/register provides no bot mitigation mechanisms, allowing malicious automated systems to flood the database.
La ruta de registro /v1/account/register no proporciona mecanismos de mitigación de bots, permitiendo que sistemas automatizados maliciosos inunden la base de datos.

Fixed AES-128-CBC keys inside the AcerConnect OTA application let attackers forge authorization credentials for arbitrary IMEI numbers. This allows unauthorized actors to list catalog items and extract protected binaries from pre-signed cloud links.

Claves AES-128-CBC fijas dentro de la aplicación AcerConnect OTA permiten a los atacantes falsificar credenciales de autorización para números IMEI arbitrarios. Esto permite a actores no autorizados listar elementos del catálogo y extraer binarios protegidos de enlaces en la nube pre-firmados.

A flaw was found in the OpenShift Pipelines operator. The tekton-scheduler-rolebinding ClusterRoleBinding grants the system:authenticated group write access to Kueue and cert-manager custom resources via the tekton-scheduler-role ClusterRole. When Kueue or cert-manager CRDs are present on the cluster, any authenticated user can disrupt workload scheduling, tamper with scheduling priorities, delete other tenants' Workload objects, or induce cert-manager to overwrite TLS Secrets including the default ingress controller certificate.

Una falla se encontró en el operador de OpenShift Pipelines. El ClusterRoleBinding tekton-scheduler-rolebinding otorga al grupo system:authenticated acceso de escritura a los recursos personalizados de Kueue y cert-manager a través del ClusterRole tekton-scheduler-role. Cuando los CRD de Kueue o cert-manager están presentes en el clúster, cualquier usuario autenticado puede interrumpir la programación de cargas de trabajo, manipular las prioridades de programación, eliminar objetos Workload de otros inquilinos o inducir a cert-manager a sobrescribir Secretos TLS, incluyendo el certificado predeterminado del controlador de entrada.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. The ansible-galaxy role install command processes dependency specifications from a role's meta/requirements.yml file. Due to improper neutralization of argument delimiters, a malicious role author can inject arbitrary git configuration flags through the src field. This allows arbitrary code execution on the machine of a user who installs the role via ansible-galaxy role install.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en ansible-core. El comando ansible-galaxy role install procesa las especificaciones de dependencia del archivo meta/requirements.yml de un rol. Debido a la neutralización incorrecta de los delimitadores de argumentos, un autor de rol malicioso puede inyectar indicadores de configuración de Git arbitrarios a través del campo src. Esto permite la ejecución de código arbitrario en la máquina de un usuario que instala el rol mediante ansible-galaxy role install.

descriptions.value: A stack-based buffer overflow flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland. A mismatch between the X server and the libXfont2 library's maximum font name length can cause a stack buffer overflow during font alias resolution. The server allocates a 256 byte stack buffer but libXfont2's alias target name length is 1024 bytes. A font alias name between 257 and 1023 bytes causes the X server to copy that name into the undersized stack buffer without further checks. This may be used to crash the server, or for privilege escalation if the X server runs as root.

A client that sets up multiple fence triggers can trigger a use-after-free function pointer call. An attacker would connect to the X server to set up a fence and await that fence, then a second X connection destroys the fence, causing the use-after-free. This may be used to crash the server, or for privilege escalation if the X server runs as root.

descriptions.value: An integer overflow flaw was found in the SASL I/O layer of 389 Directory Server (389-ds-base). In sasl_io_start_packet(), adding sizeof(uint32_t) to a crafted SASL packet length prefix of 0xFFFFFFFC causes unsigned wraparound to zero, bypassing the nsslapd-maxsasliosize limit and leading to a heap buffer overflow of up to approximately 2 megabytes of attacker-controlled data. After a successful SASL bind with integrity protection (SSF > 0), a remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE). In FreeIPA and Red Hat Identity Management deployments, any domain user with a valid Kerberos ticket, enrolled host, or service account can trigger this vulnerability over the network. This flaw is independent of CVE-2025-14905, which patched schema.c only and did not modify sasl_io.c.

descriptions.value: A heap buffer overflow vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. A flaw in the AV1 encoder's Look-Ahead Processing (LAP) mode causes the first-pass stats ring buffer wrap-around guard to be bypassed when g_lag_in_frames is set to 1 or higher. An attacker who can influence encoder configuration in a transcoding service or WebRTC session could exploit this to cause a denial of service (process crash) or potentially achieve code execution.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Foreman. The Usergroup model in Foreman does not properly validate role assignments against the calling user's permissions. This allows an authenticated user with usergroup management permissions to attach arbitrary roles, including administrative roles, to a user group and then add themselves as a member. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability leads to full privilege escalation, granting the attacker administrator-level access.

A flaw was found in Foreman. This broken access control vulnerability allows an authenticated user with host-edit permissions to retarget an existing lookup value override to a different host. This is achieved by modifying the match field through nested host attributes, effectively bypassing authorisation checks. The consequence is the potential for unauthorised modification of managed host configurations across different organisational and location boundaries.

A flaw was found in Foreman. An authenticated user with host-edit permissions could exploit a cross-tenant information disclosure vulnerability. This flaw occurs because the taxonomy_scope controller method does not properly validate organization and location IDs from nested request parameters, bypassing existing authorization checks. This allows the user to leak sensitive infrastructure metadata, including subnet topology, IP ranges, gateways, DNS servers, and VLAN IDs, from organizations and locations they are not authorized to access.

A flaw was found in foreman. Authenticated users with 'view_keypairs' permission can bypass taxonomy scoping, allowing them to download private SSH (Secure Shell) keys from other organizations by directly querying key pair IDs. This vulnerability leads to cross-tenant data exposure in multi-tenant deployments, potentially compromising sensitive information.

A heap buffer overflow flaw was found in the SASL I/O layer of 389 Directory Server
(389-ds-base). After a successful SASL bind with integrity protection (SSF > 0),
an authenticated attacker can send a specially crafted oversized LDAP UNBIND packet
that is copied into a 512-byte heap receive buffer without a bounds check in
sasl_io_recv() in sasl_io.c. This allows up to approximately 2 megabytes of
attacker-controlled data to overflow the buffer, causing a denial of service (server
crash). In FreeIPA and Red Hat Identity Management deployments, any domain user with
a valid Kerberos ticket, any enrolled host, or any service account can trigger this
vulnerability over the network after authenticating via GSSAPI.
The vulnerable code path has existed since approximately 2013 (389-ds-base 1.3.2) and
was not addressed by the CVE-2025-14905 fix, which patched a separate heap overflow
in schema.c only.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in ansible-core. The _extract_collection_from_git() function in ansible-core's concrete_artifact_manager.py constructs git clone commands without a '--' (end-of-options) separator before user-supplied URLs when installing collections from git sources. An attacker who provides a crafted collection source URI containing git argument injection payloads can achieve arbitrary command execution when a user runs 'ansible-galaxy collection install' with the malicious source. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-11332, which hardened the role install path but missed the equivalent collection install code path.

A flaw was found in openshift/oauth-proxy. The proxy sets authenticated identity headers using only dash-variant keys (X-Forwarded-User) but does not strip underscore-variant keys (X_Forwarded_User) from incoming requests. WSGI and PHP frameworks normalize both variants to the same variable, allowing an authenticated low-privilege user to smuggle a forged identity that may override the legitimate authenticated identity in the upstream application.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en openshift/oauth-proxy. El proxy establece encabezados de identidad autenticada utilizando solo claves con variantes de guion (X-Forwarded-User) pero no elimina las claves con variantes de guion bajo (X_Forwarded_User) de las solicitudes entrantes. Los frameworks WSGI y PHP normalizan ambas variantes a la misma variable, permitiendo a un usuario autenticado con bajos privilegios introducir clandestinamente una identidad falsificada que puede anular la identidad autenticada legítima en la aplicación ascendente.

A flaw was found in Dogtag PKI's ACME responder where the HTTP-01 challenge validator accepts IP address literals as dns identifiers and follows HTTP redirects without validating that the target is a public address. An unauthenticated ACME account holder can exploit this to perform server-side request forgery (SSRF), making the Dogtag server send HTTP GET requests to internal network services. With the InMemory database backend, the response body of internal targets is disclosed to the attacker through the ACME challenge error.

descriptions.value: A stack buffer overflow flaw was found in 389 Directory Server (389-ds-base). The get_ruvelement_from_berval() function in repl5_ruv.c copies digit characters from a network-supplied RUV berval into a fixed 16-byte stack buffer without bounds checking. A remote unauthenticated attacker can crash the LDAP server by sending a crafted StartNSDS50ReplicationRequest extended operation containing a replica ID field with more than 16 digit characters. The overflow occurs during payload decoding, before any authorization check. Stack protectors limit impact to denial of service.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Multicluster Engine for Kubernetes ClusterCurator controller. A tenant administrator with namespace-scoped privileges can exploit this vulnerability by creating a namespaced ClusterCurator. This action inadvertently grants the tenant administrator the ability to mint a token for a ServiceAccount with cluster-wide administrative authority. This leads to a privilege escalation, allowing the tenant administrator to gain full control over the cluster.

Se encontró una falla en el controlador ClusterCurator de Multicluster Engine para Kubernetes. Un administrador de inquilinos con privilegios de ámbito de espacio de nombres puede explotar esta vulnerabilidad al crear un ClusterCurator con ámbito de espacio de nombres. Esta acción otorga inadvertidamente al administrador de inquilinos la capacidad de acuñar un token para una ServiceAccount con autoridad administrativa de ámbito de clúster. Esto conduce a una escalada de privilegios, lo que permite al administrador de inquilinos obtener control total sobre el clúster.

A flaw was found in openshift/oauth-proxy. On paths configured to bypass authentication (skip-auth-regex), the proxy forwards client-supplied identity headers (X-Forwarded-User, X-Forwarded-Email, X-Forwarded-Access-Token) to the upstream application without stripping them. An unauthenticated attacker can inject forged identity headers on whitelisted paths.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en openshift/oauth-proxy. En rutas configuradas para omitir la autenticación (skip-auth-regex), el proxy reenvía los encabezados de identidad proporcionados por el cliente (X-Forwarded-User, X-Forwarded-Email, X-Forwarded-Access-Token) a la aplicación ascendente sin eliminarlos. Un atacante no autenticado puede inyectar encabezados de identidad falsificados en rutas permitidas.

A flaw was found in multicluster-global-hub. The manager component improperly validates the source identity of incoming CloudEvents on Kafka status topics. A remote attacker, after compromising a managed hub and obtaining its Kafka client certificate, can manipulate the self-asserted source identity. This allows the attacker to falsify or delete critical data, such as compliance, inventory, and cluster health information, belonging to other hubs in the database.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en multicluster-global-hub. El componente gestor valida incorrectamente la identidad de origen de los CloudEvents entrantes en los temas de estado de Kafka. Un atacante remoto, después de comprometer un hub gestionado y obtener su certificado de cliente Kafka, puede manipular la identidad de origen autoafirmada. Esto permite al atacante falsificar o eliminar datos críticos, como información de cumplimiento, inventario y estado del clúster, perteneciente a otros hubs en la base de datos.

A flaw was found in multicluster-global-hub. During a ManagedClusterMigration, the system incorrectly grants all managed hubs read access to a shared communication topic. This allows a compromised managed hub to intercept and collect sensitive bootstrap kubeconfigs, which contain API server tokens intended for other hubs. These tokens have an extended validity of approximately 9.86 years, significantly increasing the risk of unauthorized access and information disclosure to other managed clusters.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en multicluster-global-hub. Durante una ManagedClusterMigration, el sistema concede incorrectamente a todos los hubs gestionados acceso de lectura a un tema de comunicación compartido. Esto permite a un hub gestionado comprometido interceptar y recopilar kubeconfigs de arranque sensibles, que contienen tokens del servidor API destinados a otros hubs. Estos tokens tienen una validez extendida de aproximadamente 9.86 años, lo que aumenta significativamente el riesgo de acceso no autorizado y revelación de información a otros clusters gestionados.

A flaw was found in Picketlink Federation SAML; the unsolcited response handler would accept forged assertions with no verification or validation, permitting an unauthed attacker to authenticate as any principal in any role. This could lead to information disclosure, access to restricted operations, or other flaws.

descriptions.value: A Server-Side Request Forgery and supply chain flaw was found in the OpenShift Console Helm catalog proxy. A namespace tenant can plant a ProjectHelmChartRepository with an arbitrary URL that the console pod fetches server-side, bypassing tenant egress restrictions. Combined with catalog metadata poisoning and admin-mediated chart installation, this enables privilege escalation.

Se encontró una falsificación de petición del lado del servidor y un fallo en la cadena de suministro en el proxy del catálogo Helm de OpenShift Console. Un inquilino de espacio de nombres puede introducir un ProjectHelmChartRepository con una URL arbitraria que el pod de la consola obtiene del lado del servidor, eludiendo las restricciones de salida del inquilino. Combinado con el envenenamiento de metadatos del catálogo y la instalación de gráficos mediada por el administrador, esto permite la escalada de privilegios.

A flaw was found in the oauth-server component. This open redirect vulnerability occurs when the 'then' parameter in the grant approval handler is not properly validated. A remote attacker can craft a malicious URL that, when approved or denied by an authenticated user, redirects them to an attacker-controlled website. This could enable phishing attacks, potentially tricking users into revealing sensitive information.

Se encontró una falla en el componente oauth-server. Esta vulnerabilidad de redirección abierta ocurre cuando el parámetro ’then’ en el gestor de aprobación de concesión no se valida correctamente. Un atacante remoto puede crear una URL maliciosa que, cuando es aprobada o denegada por un usuario autenticado, los redirige a un sitio web controlado por el atacante. Esto podría permitir ataques de phishing, engañando potencialmente a los usuarios para que revelen información sensible.

A flaw was found in WildFly Elytron. Password hashing and verification normalize input with Unicode NFKC, which can collapse fullwidth characters to ASCII equivalents. A remote attacker can more easily guess affected passwords by using an ASCII-only dictionary against accounts whose passwords were intended to include those non-ASCII characters, leading to unauthorized access.

Se encontró un fallo en WildFly Elytron. El hash y la verificación de contraseñas normalizan la entrada con Unicode NFKC, lo que puede colapsar caracteres de ancho completo a sus equivalentes ASCII. Un atacante remoto puede adivinar más fácilmente las contraseñas afectadas al usar un diccionario exclusivamente ASCII contra cuentas cuyas contraseñas estaban destinadas a incluir esos caracteres no ASCII, lo que lleva a un acceso no autorizado.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Foreman. The template revision endpoint does not enforce object-level authorization when retrieving an audited template revision. An authenticated, low privileged user with a template-related permission, such as view_ptables, can obtain historical template contents belonging to another organization or location by supplying the corresponding audit ID. This can result in unauthorized disclosure of historical template contents, which may contain sensitive configuration information, credentials, or other secrets. The REST API revision endpoints correctly restrict this lookup.

A flaw was found in the Qute template engine, which is used by Quarkus to generate dynamic content like HTML pages or emails. The issue exists in the component responsible for looking up data values (ReflectionValueResolver), which fails to properly block access to sensitive Java internal functions when processing certain data types like Enums. An attacker who can provide or influence the template text can exploit this bypass to take control of the server by executing unauthorized commands.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in RESTEasy's SourceProvider. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to perform an unauthenticated remote file read. By sending a specially crafted XML body with a DOCTYPE declaration referencing external entities to an endpoint that accepts application/xml and returns Source or StreamSource, the server can be tricked into resolving the entity and including sensitive file contents in the HTTP response. This is due to the SourceProvider.writeTo() method creating a SAXParser without disabling external entity resolution, leading to an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability.

descriptions.value: A heap-based buffer overflow was found in Corosync's Totem Process Group (totempg) message reassembly. When processing fragmented multicast messages, the buffer used to reassemble fragments lacks a runtime bounds check in release builds. A network-adjacent attacker able to send crafted multicast protocol messages to the cluster could cause a heap buffer overflow with attacker-controlled data. This can crash the Corosync daemon, causing a denial of service to the entire cluster, and may potentially allow further exploitation given sufficient heap-corruption control.

descriptions.value: A heap buffer overflow flaw was found in the SASL I/O layer of 389 Directory Server (389-ds-base). In sasl_io_start_packet(), the wrapped-record length read from the wire is validated only against an upper bound. A small wire length (0, 1, or 2) produces an encrypted_buffer_count below the already-consumed encrypted_buffer_offset, causing an unsigned subtraction underflow in sasl_io_read_packet(). PR_Recv is then requested to read approximately 4 GiB into a 1024-byte heap buffer, resulting in a heap buffer overflow with attacker-controlled content. After a successful SASL bind with integrity protection (SSF > 0), a remote authenticated attacker can cause a denial of service or potentially achieve remote code execution. This flaw is distinct from CVE-2026-11774, whose fix only guards against upper-bound overflow.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. During SASL PLAIN authentication, a stale identity carried in a Cyrus SASL auxiliary property from a prior failed bind attempt can be installed on a connection following a subsequent, unrelated successful bind, regardless of which SASL mechanism completes that second bind. An attacker can send a SASL PLAIN bind as cn=Directory Manager with an incorrect password, then complete a SASL ANONYMOUS bind on the same connection, causing the server to grant Directory Manager authority without any valid credentials. A variant using a valid low-privileged account's own successful bind instead of an anonymous one is also possible.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Dynamic Client Registration service of Keycloak, an open-source identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when a user with the view-clients role accesses the client registration endpoint to retrieve client details. Due to a failure to mask sensitive information, the service returns the client's confidential secret in cleartext. This could allow a read-only administrator to obtain full access to the affected client's account and potentially escalate their privileges within the realm.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Acer Agent Service component included with NitroSense and PredatorSense. The vulnerability is caused by the use of a hard-coded AES encryption key within the software. Under certain circumstances, a local attacker may be able to use the embedded key to access protected information or perform unauthorized actions.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Acer Agent Service component included with NitroSense and PredatorSense. The socket handshake process does not properly require authentication before granting access to the service. Under certain circumstances, an unauthorized connection may be established, potentially allowing access to functionality that should be restricted.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Acer Agent Service component included with NitroSense and PredatorSense. Insufficient access controls within a privileged service may allow an authenticated local user to perform unauthorized registry operations. In certain situations, this could lead to privilege escalation or compromise of the affected system.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Acer System Monitoring component included with NitroSense and PredatorSense. The vulnerability is caused by the use of a hard-coded AES encryption key within the software. Under certain circumstances, a local attacker may be able to use the embedded key to access protected information or perform unauthorized actions.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Acer System Monitoring component included with NitroSense and PredatorSense. A WebSocket service was configured to listen on all network interfaces, which may expose the service to unintended network access.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Acer System Monitoring component included with NitroSense and PredatorSense. The WebSocket handshake process does not properly require authentication before allowing connections to the service. Under certain circumstances, unauthorized access to service functionality may be possible.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Acer System Monitoring component included with NitroSense and PredatorSense. Insufficient access controls within a privileged Named Pipe service may allow an authenticated local user to perform unauthorized registry operations. In certain situations, this could lead to privilege escalation or compromise of the affected system.

A vulnerability has been identified in the Acer System Monitoring component included with NitroSense and PredatorSense due to insufficient access controls in a privileged service. An authenticated local user may be able to access the service and perform unauthorized registry modifications, potentially resulting in local privilege escalation.

A flaw was found in RESTEasy's CorsFilter, which, when configured to allow all origins ("*"), reflects the request's Origin header back in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permissive cross-origin policy allows a malicious website to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read authenticated responses from a victim's session, resulting in a loss of confidentiality.

This allows the attacker to read sensitive `*.json` files from the pod filesystem, including plugin manifests and configuration files. Furthermore, this flaw can enable path traversal against registered dynamic-plugin backends.

An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

descriptions.value: A trust-boundary flaw in CRI-O's sandbox state persistence allows attacker-influenced pod metadata to overwrite CRI-O's own reserved sandbox bookkeeping; once reloaded as trusted after a restart, a later container recreate in that sandbox can expose a host-side runtime-management resource inside the container, enabling container escape.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The Red Hat Satellite /unattended/provision API endpoint is vulnerable to an authentication bypass due to a semantic logic flaw in host_verifier.rb. The application verifies the database state of a provisioning token rather than its actual presence in the incoming HTTP request. Because a host actively undergoing provisioning has an unexpired token in the database, the server's valid_host_token? method evaluates to true, granting access to the kickstart template even if the requester provides no token at all in the URL.

A flaw was found in Foreman. A command injection vulnerability exists in the foreman-rake errors:fetch_log task. The request_id parameter is passed to an underlying system command (typically grep) without adequate shell neutralization. While the task is intended to fetch specific log entries, an attacker with sudo permissions to execute this rake task can inject shell metacharacters (such as ;, ", or |) to break out of the intended command and execute arbitrary code.

A flaw was found in Foreman. OS command injection vulnerabilities exist in the foreman-rake db:dump and db:import_dump tasks. The application fails to properly sanitize user-supplied input in the destination parameter (during backups) and the file parameter (during imports) before passing them to a Ruby system() call for execution. An attacker with permissions to execute foreman-rake (e.g., via a restricted sudo configuration) can append malicious shell commands to the provided file paths.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The foreman-rake initialization logic in /usr/share/foreman/config/settings.rb contains a vulnerable code pattern where configuration data is processed through two distinct executable layers. This creates a multi-stage execution chain that allows for both Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) and insecure deserialization. This vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, total infrastructure compromise and supply chain risk.

A flaw was found in Foreman. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker with low-level read permissions to achieve arbitrary code execution on the underlying server. By manipulating the permitted methods list within the template rendering engine, an attacker can bypass the safemode sandbox isolation and execute unauthorized commands directly on the host system.

A flaw was found in Foreman. This vulnerability allows an authenticated user with low-level Viewer permissions to cause unauthorized information disclosure by submitting requests to template preview endpoints. By exploiting this issue, the user can access sensitive data, such as host root passwords. Furthermore, under insecure system configurations where Safemode protections are disabled, the flaw may allow the user to execute arbitrary commands as the Foreman system account.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The foreman-tail utility is vulnerable to OS command injection due to the unsafe use of the eval command. The script takes user-supplied arguments and incorporates them directly into a string that is then executed by eval to expand file paths. Because the input is not sanitized or quoted, a local attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g., ;, &, |) to execute arbitrary system commands.

A flaw was found in rubygem-hammer_cli. A command injection vulnerability exists in Hammer CLI and the Railties (Ruby on Rails) component distributed with Satellite due to the insecure interpolation of the $EDITOR environment variable into the Ruby system() method. By passing a single interpolated string to system(), the application invokes a system shell (/bin/sh) that interprets shell metacharacters (e.g., ;, |, &).

A flaw has been found in **permission filters** in the **foreman** package. The API loads a filter by its identifier and does not apply the search limit on the caller's permission. A low-privileged network attacker or user must already be allowed to delete filters for one role only. They can delete filters that belong to other unlocked roles. Those other roles then lose the access the deleted filters had granted.

A flaw was found in libblockdev. The bd_fs_ntfs_set_label() and bd_fs_vfat_set_label() functions pass caller-supplied label values as bare positional arguments to the ntfslabel and fatlabel utilities without end-of-options separators or input validation for values beginning with a dash. This allows a label starting with '-' to be interpreted as a command-line flag by the spawned tool, potentially bypassing safety checks or causing unintended operations. This is reachable by unprivileged local users through the udisks2 Filesystem.SetLabel() D-Bus method without administrator authentication.

A flaw was found in Nautilus. When a removable drive or disk image is unmounted or ejected, Nautilus prompts the user to empty the trash without verifying whether the trash directory paths are symbolic links. An attacker can exploit this flaw by tricking a user into mounting a crafted storage volume and confirming the prompt to empty the trash, leading to the arbitrary deletion of files accessible to that user.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes (RHACS). The Central SAML authentication ACS endpoint does not retain used SAML assertion or response identifiers to prevent replay. An attacker who obtains a valid, unexpired signed SAML response can submit it multiple times and receive distinct Central authentication tokens for the mapped identity.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the SAML HTTP-Redirect binding implementation of Keycloak. The issue occurs because the server processes percent-encoded parameter names (like %53AMLResponse) while the signature verification logic only checks literal parameter names. An attacker can use this discrepancy to provide a crafted, unsigned SAML message that the server processes instead of a legitimately signed one, leading to full account takeover of federated users.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak server's client management component. When a client is created or imported with authorization services enabled, the system fails to properly clear an internal session attribute used during the setup process. This allows an authenticated attacker with client management permissions to bypass security controls and upload a malicious JavaScript policy, which is then executed on the server when an authorization request is made. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to run arbitrary code on the server, potentially compromising the entire system.

A flaw was found in ansible-core's ansible.builtin.git module. The module
invokes git (ls-remote, clone, fetch) with the repository URL as a positional
argument and without a "--" separator, so a repository URL that begins with a
dash is interpreted by git as a command-line option. A caller that passes an
attacker-controlled repository URL to the module can trigger argument
injection (for example --upload-pack/--exec), resulting in arbitrary command
execution on the host running the module.

descriptions.value: Fluxion before 6.39 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the fluxion.sh target scanner, which decodes access point ESSIDs with eval after escaping only single quotes. Attackers within Wi-Fi range can broadcast an access point with a crafted SSID to execute commands as root when the operator scans or selects it.

A flaw was found in cpio. A local user can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering a stack-based buffer overflow when creating archives in tar or ustar formats. When archiving files owned by users or groups with names exceeding 32 characters, cpio copies these names into fixed-size memory without verifying their length. This unbounded copy corrupts stack memory and causes the application to crash.

A flaw was found in Foreman. An authenticated user with view_hosts privileges can retrieve rendered provisioning template content for a host via the hosts template API endpoint, disclosing sensitive data such as the host root password. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-96659, which hardened the web UI preview path but left the API host-template render path authorized for Viewer-level users.

A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::PersonalAccessTokensController, where Foreman::Controller::UserAware#find_user resolves the target account using User.find(params[:user_id]) without applying the required parent-user authorization check. An attacker with the create_personal_access_tokens permission can therefore invoke POST /api/v2/users/:user_id/personal_access_tokens with another user’s ID and create a Personal Access Token on their behalf. The resulting plaintext token is returned in the API response, while PersonalAccessToken#check_permissions_after_save only validates create_personal_access_tokens on the token and does not enforce edit_users authorization on the target user. The attacker can then use the forged token to authenticate as the victim, potentially resulting in complete account takeover, including administrator accounts.

A missing authorization check has been found in the user_mail_notifications function in mail_notifications_controller.rb of the mail notification API in the foreman package. The action returns another user's notification settings when only the generic view permission for mail notifications is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can view mail notifications can request any user id and read that user's subscription choices and stored mail search strings.

A missing authorization check has been found in the find_user function in user_aware.rb of the SSH key API in the foreman package. The create action attaches a new public key to the user id in the request without checking that the caller may edit that user. A low-privileged network attacker or user who already holds permission to create SSH keys can add their key to another user's account. That key is then stored with the victim and can be used by features that export that user's SSH keys.

A flaw was found in abrt. abrt-server trusts a client-supplied PID when creating problem dumps over abrt.socket and, running as root, copies that process's /proc data (including environ) into a dump directory owned by the connecting unprivileged user. This allows a local attacker to read environment variables and related metadata of other users' or root processes when abrtd is running.

WLA DX 9.7 before 10.8 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in parse_data_blocks() in wlalink/analyze.c that copies section namespaces without length checks. Attackers can supply a crafted object or library file with a namespace longer than 255 bytes or unterminated to overflow the 256-byte stack buffer when linked.

A flaw was found in the file-xmc plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted XMC image file, the plugin does not properly validate the comment subtype before using it as an array index. This missing validation leads to out-of-bounds memory access, invalid free and use-after-free issues. This vulnerability can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

A flaw was found in hypershift-addon. Due to an overly permissive role-based access control (RBAC) configuration that grants permissions to all authenticated users rather than restricting them to the addon service, a low-privileged authenticated user can view, modify, or delete managed cluster resources. This improper authorization allows unauthorized users to alter or disrupt clusters across the entire managed fleet.

THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Cookie and Authorization headers by redirecting requests to another host. Attackers controlling the scanned target or abusing an open redirect can make RedirectHandler.http_error_302 forward session cookies or bearer tokens to an attacker-controlled host.

A flaw was found in KubeVirt/containerized-data-importer. When a VirtualMachine with an embedded DataVolumeTemplate carrying the cdi.kubevirt.io/storage.checkStaticVolume annotation and a cross-namespace clone source is created by a tenant, the service-account clone authorization check can be bypassed, allowing a PVC from another namespace to be cloned into the tenant's namespace without the required permissions. This can result in cross-tenant data disclosure.

dsniff through 2.5a2 contains an integer underflow in decode_sniffer() in decode_sniffer.c that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write past the global obuf buffer. Attackers can send a UDP datagram to port 2001 on a monitored segment with a 4096-byte string, disabling base64_pton bounds checks to corrupt memory and crash dsniff.

Wfuzz through 3.1.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious target servers to inject script by returning crafted links written unescaped into HTML reports. When the links script and html printer are used, attacker-supplied href values close the unquoted anchor tag and execute JavaScript when the operator opens the report.

Missing authorization in the Elastic AI Assistant for Security in Kibana can allow an authenticated assistant user to permanently delete a shared or global Security AI Assistant conversation owned by another user in the same space. The individual-delete path can treat read access to a shared conversation as permission to delete it without checking ownership. The deleted conversation history is lost to its legitimate owner.

hping3 through commit 3547c76 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in display_ipopt() that allows remote attackers to overflow the static 40-byte old_rr buffer via a crafted IP Record Route option. Attackers acting as the probed host, on-path, or spoofing the target can send replies with option lengths up to 255 to hping3 running with -G/--rroute, corrupting global memory and crashing hping3.

Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.

The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.

An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.

Pydantic AI Harness's PlaywrightBrowser enforces its egress policy on HTTP requests and page WebSockets, but not on WebRTC or WebTransport connections, WebSockets opened with WebSocketStream, or the requests the browser itself sends for FedCM. A page the agent opens can make the browser send WebRTC (STUN and TURN), WebTransport and WebSocketStream traffic, and FedCM requests, to hosts and ports that the policy refuses, including under a policy that limits every request kind to an allowlist.

This affects applications that use PlaywrightBrowser to open pages an attacker can influence. The traffic is each protocol's connection setup, sent to a destination the page chooses. A page can learn whether a target answers a STUN request. No response body from an ordinary internal service was readable through WebRTC, WebTransport or FedCM. A WebSocketStream is an ordinary WebSocket that the WebSocket guard does not see, opened from a page, a frame or a worker, and the page reads what the server sends, including from a private address. Chromium's Local Network Access blocks WebTransport from public pages to private addresses, but does not block WebRTC.

A FedCM call (navigator.credentials.get with an identity provider) makes the browser fetch the provider's /.well-known/web-identity, config, accounts and client metadata URLs. The page chooses the config URL's path and the client ID, so it can send data to a host outside allowed_domains or listed in blocked_domains. The accounts request carries the provider's cookies from the browser profile. FedCM requires a provider origin that is HTTPS or loopback.

The assumed attacker is a third party with no access to the application who controls script on a page the agent opens.

Under an enforced egress policy, which is the default, pydantic-ai-harness 0.74.0 removes RTCPeerConnection, webkitRTCPeerConnection, WebTransport, WebSocketStream, IdentityCredential and IdentityProvider from every page and frame, refuses FedCM calls to navigator.credentials.get, and launches Chromium with FedCM and WebSocketStream turned off. These paths stay outside the policy: WebTransport from workers; WebSocketStream from workers in a browser reached over cdp_url; WebTransport in sandboxed iframes that Chromium runs in their own process (headless=False and cdp_url); and documents loaded before attachment under cdp_context='default'.

Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.74.0 or later. For the paths the upgrade leaves open, and until you upgrade, run the browser behind a network egress filter that also covers UDP, or do not open untrusted URLs with PlaywrightBrowser.

It treated any URL containing a backslash as having no host, and it allows script and asset requests with no host. A page script could therefore add a backslash to a URL's query to send requests to private addresses, to hosts outside allowed_domains, and to hosts in blocked_domains.

This affects applications that use PlaywrightBrowser to open pages or follow instructions an attacker can influence. It applies to fetch, XHR, sendBeacon, WebSocket and passive asset requests. Navigation and frames were not affected. A policy that limits every request kind to an allowlist did not prevent data from being sent to another host.

Responses from private services could be read only when the service permits cross-origin reads or accepts the WebSocket connection. Current Chromium versions separately block many requests from public pages to private addresses, but not requests between public hosts, and not when the browser runs behind a forward proxy.

The assumed attacker is a third party with no access to the application who controls script on a page the agent opens, or content that steers the agent's browser tools.

Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.74.0 or later. Until then, enforce egress outside the browser with a firewall or a filtering proxy, and do not rely on the browser's domain lists for untrusted pages.

The Widgets for Social Photo Feed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'widget-id' shortcode attribute of the [trustindex-feed] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 1.8.3 This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping in the registerWidget() function, which concatenates the raw shortcode attribute directly into a double-quoted JavaScript string literal that is then enqueued via wp_add_inline_script() and rendered in wp_footer/admin_footer. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (via wp-admin/post.php add_meta → post_meta key 'my_field')' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor can store a raw script payload in a custom field on their own draft and cause it to execute in an administrator's or editor's authenticated browser session when they preview or publish the post.

The Beautiful taxonomy filters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'term_name (reflected from DB)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an attacker to first create a maliciously-named taxonomy term as an Author-level user; the nonce required to trigger execution is publicly emitted on any front-end page displaying the taxonomy filter widget, making the injected payload reachable by completely unauthenticated visitors.

The Ninja Tables – Responsive Table Builder for Data, Pricing & Product Tables plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 'dateFormat' column metadata parameter in versions up to, and including, 5.5.1 This is due to insufficient escaping on the stored 'dateFormat' value in DefaultProvider::orderByJsonQuery(); convertDateFormatToMysql() only performs str_replace on date-format tokens and leaves SQL metacharacters (including single quotes) intact, after which the value is concatenated directly into an orderByRaw() ORDER BY clause inside single quotes. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database; the payload is stored in the _ninja_table_columns post meta and executed on every unauthenticated request to the wp_ajax_ninja_tables_public_action AJAX endpoint when the table uses sorting_type='by_column' with a date column.

descriptions.value: The Funnelforms Free – Multi Step Form, Contact Form & Lead Funnel Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'document.settings.heading' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable on standard single-site WordPress installs only when the DISALLOW_UNFILTERED_HTML constant is set, the site is a WordPress multisite network (where administrators lack the unfiltered_html capability by default), or an administrator has explicitly granted the funnelforms_edit_forms capability to a lower-privileged role. Exploitation by attackers with administrator-level access and above requires that the site is a WordPress multisite install (site admins automatically lack unfiltered_html). On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with custom-level access and above.

descriptions.value:
Bizum Pay for Android incorporates static values within the APK to authenticate and sign requests to its API, including those for user registration. These values are common across different installations and can be extracted from the APK. An attacker who obtains the application could reuse them to generate requests that the server accepts as authenticated. The potential scope of these requests was limited to querying auxiliary information and certain configuration statuses. Under no circumstances could they generate unauthorised payments via Bizum Pay, nor could they carry out illegitimate activations of the app (which always require access to the customer’s banking channels, thereby protecting them from this type of potential vulnerability). Furthermore, requests are always limited to a set number of attempts and are closely monitored to prevent potential mass queries.

descriptions.value: The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in versions up to, and including, 4.11 This is due to the Admin_Page::page() callback dispatching methods named directly by the $_REQUEST['action'] parameter via call_user_func([$this, $action]) without verifying a nonce: the only nonce check lives in process_action() (admin_init), which prefixes the action with 'process_' before dispatching, so an attacker who supplies action=process_delete causes process_action() to look up the nonexistent 'process_process_delete' method and bail without ever calling wp_verify_nonce(), while page() subsequently invokes the real process_delete() (and other process_* methods such as process_spam, process_status_change, process_edit) with no CSRF token of its own. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary contacts, change contact opt-in status (including marking contacts as spam, which also appends their IP to the site-wide disallowed_keys option), and perform other state-changing actions via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator (or any user holding the relevant Groundhogg capability such as delete_contacts/edit_contacts) into performing an action such as clicking on a link.

affectedData.product: Groundhogg — AI CRM, Newsletters, and Marketing Automation

descriptions.value: The AI Engine – MCP Server & AI Chatbot for WordPress, with Claude, ChatGPT & Gemini plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Limited Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.4 via the `url` parameter of the `/mwai/v1/helpers/create_image` REST API endpoint. The vulnerability exists because the `add_image_from_url()` function applies the `get_allowed_mime_types()` extension allow-list only on the custom-filename branch; when the request omits a `filename` value, the empty-filename branch derives the stored file's extension directly from the URL basename via `sanitize_file_name()` without any MIME or extension validation, then writes the downloaded response body verbatim to the WordPress uploads directory via `file_put_contents()`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Editor-level access and above to place attacker-controlled HTML, SVG, or JavaScript files into `wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/` under an attacker-chosen extension, enabling stored cross-site scripting against any administrator who opens the resulting attachment URL. The download routine accepts any HTTP response whose `Content-Type` header begins with `image/`, a value freely controlled by the attacker-owned origin server, meaning the written content need not be a valid image.

affectedData.product: AI Engine – MCP Server & AI Chatbot for WordPress, with Claude, ChatGPT & Gemini

descriptions.value: The ShopMagic – email automation for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.5 Although `CurrentCustomer::encode_tracking_data()` appends an md5 hash to the `shopmagic_visitor_<COOKIEHASH>` cookie to make it tamper-resistant, `CookiePersistence::get_tracking_data()` returns the raw `json_decode()`'d cookie value directly without computing or verifying that hash, leaving the cookie's `user_id`, `email`, and `meta` fields fully under attacker control. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to forge the visitor cookie — which is predictable because its name is derived as `md5(siteurl)` from the public site URL — and submit it to the unprotected `wp_ajax_nopriv_capture_email_url` endpoint (which is registered without a nonce check or capability check) to impersonate any WordPress user including administrators in ShopMagic's customer-identity context, and to overwrite the stored profile metadata — including name, phone number, and billing address — of any existing guest record in `wp_shopmagic_guest` and `wp_shopmagic_guest_meta` via `GuestManager::save()`.

The CubeWP Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.32 This is due to the `cubewp_frontend_role_caps()` function, registered on the `user_has_cap` filter, which excludes REST API requests via a `REST_REQUEST` guard but omits a corresponding `XMLRPC_REQUEST` check, causing it to unconditionally widen capabilities for any Subscriber or Contributor on XML-RPC and admin-ajax.php request paths. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access and above to escalate their privileges to the full Contributor role capability set — gaining `edit_posts`, `delete_posts`, and `read` — allowing them to create, edit, and delete posts through core XML-RPC methods such as `wp.newPost`. Critically, the capability widening is not scoped to CubeWP's own submission handlers but applies globally to all core capability gates on affected request paths, meaning any Subscriber account can exploit this with a single standard XML-RPC call and no CubeWP-specific interaction. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive every capability defined for the Contributor role.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file[files][]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the affected package uses a link template containing the [play_button] shortcode, such as the bundled 'With Audio Preview' template, since the vulnerable audioPlayer() output path is only triggered when that placeholder is rendered.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file[page_template], file[files][]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 via the 'file[page_template]' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The malicious page_template value is stored when an Author creates or edits a package post, and the inclusion is triggered on any subsequent page view of the package permalink, meaning the include() can be fired by unauthenticated visitors after the payload is planted.

The Music Player for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.4 via the '_downloadable_files' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Staging the attack requires storing a crafted downloadable file URL against a product, which requires the edit_products capability (Shop Manager or above); however, triggering the file read via the ?wcmp-action=play handler is fully unauthenticated once the crafted URL is saved to a published product.

JobRouter Premium, version 2025.1.11, has a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Favorites feature. An authenticated user with low privileges can inject JavaScript code that is persistently stored on the server. When other users access the affected page, the code executes in their browsers. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the victim, access sensitive information, or compromise the integrity of their sessions.

In Eclipse Ditto versions 0.3.0-M1 through 3.8.15 and 3.9.0 through 3.9.9, the JavaScript payload mapper of the connectivity service executes user-supplied mapping scripts in a Mozilla Rhino engine without a ClassShutter. This allows a user permitted to create or modify connections (by default the Ditto DevOps realm) to execute arbitrary code in the connectivity service, gaining access to its credentials and to the Ditto cluster.

The Timetics – Appointment Booking Calendar & Scheduling System plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification of data and user account creation in versions up to, and including, 1.0.67 This is due to the public `POST /wp-json/timetics/v1/bookings` route being registered with `permission_callback => function () { return true; }` and the handler (`create_item()` → `save_bookings()` → `booking_appointment()`) passing the attacker-controlled `email` directly into `Customer::make()`, which (a) grants the `timetics-customer` role to any existing WordPress user matched by email — including administrators and staff — and overwrites that account's `first_name`/`last_name` user meta, and (b) calls `wp_insert_user()` with role `timetics-customer` when the email is new, regardless of the site's `users_can_register` setting. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to create arbitrary WordPress user accounts, assign the `timetics-customer` role to existing accounts (including administrators), and overwrite their profile metadata.

The MoreConvert Wishlist for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'empty_icon' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom_text (shortcode attribute of [vc_cta])' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used to handle OpenID Connect authentication flows. The issue occurs because the security check that prevents attackers from pre-seeding security parameters in a redirect URL can be bypassed by adding an extra question mark character to the parameter name. This allows an attacker to trick a user's browser into using an attacker-controlled login code. As a result, a victim may be unknowingly logged into an attacker's account, leading to account confusion or the exposure of sensitive data entered by the victim.

A flaw was found in the SAML identity brokering component of Keycloak. When Keycloak is configured to use a database with case-insensitive collation, it may incorrectly match a SAML subject name to an existing user account if the names differ only by case. This issue allows an attacker to log in as a different user by providing a case-distinct version of a victim's username in a signed SAML assertion, leading to unauthorized account access.

Relative Path Traversal vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_lambda (ExAws.Lambda module) allows an attacker to redirect an AWS Lambda control-plane request at an unintended resource by injecting path traversal sequences into a caller-supplied identifier.

This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/lambda.ex and program routines ExAws.Lambda.add_permission/5, ExAws.Lambda.delete_event_source_mapping/1, ExAws.Lambda.delete_function/1, ExAws.Lambda.get_event_source_mapping/1, ExAws.Lambda.get_function/1, ExAws.Lambda.get_function_configuration/1, ExAws.Lambda.get_policy/1, ExAws.Lambda.invoke/4, ExAws.Lambda.invoke_async/2, ExAws.Lambda.remove_permission/2, ExAws.Lambda.update_event_source_mapping/2, ExAws.Lambda.update_function_code/2, ExAws.Lambda.update_function_configuration/2.

ExAws.Lambda builds every request path by interpolating caller-supplied identifiers (function names, ARNs, UUIDs, statement IDs) directly into the URL with plain string interpolation, without percent-encoding or validation. The shared request helper only encodes query parameters, never the path, so path metacharacters such as / and .. reach the wire unchanged. An application that passes an untrusted or user-influenced identifier into an ExAws.Lambda operation can therefore have its request steered at a different Lambda resource: a ../ segment climbs out of the intended /2015-03-31/functions/<name> slot and, once the .. is normalized by the HTTP client or the AWS endpoint, addresses a sibling function in the same account. The signed credentials and the HTTP method are unchanged, so the request still succeeds against the wrong resource. Affected operations include function deletion, invocation, configuration updates, and permission changes. Applications that only pass hardcoded or strictly validated identifiers are not affected.

This issue affects ex_aws_lambda: from 2.0.1 before 2.2.0.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache SkyWalking BanyanDB.



Uncontrolled resource consumption in Apache SkyWalking BanyanDB's query API allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause the server to exhaust memory and terminate. A query request can specify an arbitrarily large result limit and offset, which the server uses to pre-allocate result buffers without an upper bound; a single request may force an allocation of tens of gigabytes and cause the process to be killed



This issue affects Apache SkyWalking BanyanDB: from 0.11.0 before 0.11.1.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.11.1, which fixes the issue.
